races.title: State Assembly, District 19
races.note: The top two finishers from the Nov 3, 2026 count. Everyone else in this race is coming.

cands.name: Catherine Stefani
cands.bio: Attorney and Democrat who has represented Assembly District 19 since December 2024. Earlier she was a Contra Costa County prosecutor, a legislative aide, San Francisco County Clerk (appointed 2016), and a San Francisco Supervisor for District 2 (2018–2024).

endorsements.text: California Federation of Labor Unions, AFL-CIO (2026 election)

cands.gaps: We found no stated position or action by Stefani on data centers, eliminating homestead property taxes, limits on investor or foreign land buyers, H-1B visas or immigration enforcement, or school vouchers and charters. Her campaign site promises more funding for schools and teachers but does not mention a pay raise or school choice. The Ballotpedia list of bills she has sponsored in the Assembly came through empty, so her Assembly bills are not described here. Her claims to have authored the first ghost gun ban and to have passed red flag legislation as a Supervisor come from her own campaign materials and were not confirmed in a primary record. Ballotpedia says she did not complete its 2026 candidate survey.

local.label: Roots 100: Ballotpedia lists her birthplace as San Francisco, and her campaign site says she grew up in Merced in the Central Valley and has lived in San Francisco for more than two decades.

land.label: 1 documented position for data centers or more development; 1 protecting land

score.why: Raised $0, under $5,000 for this office: too little money to score fairly.

qual.background: Served on the San Francisco Board of Supervisors (2018–2024) and in the Assembly (2024–present). Earlier she was a deputy district attorney, a policy analyst or aide to Assembly Speaker Herb Wesson, San Jose Vice Mayor Cindy Chavez and the California Department of Justice, a legislative aide to two San Francisco supervisors, and San Francisco County Clerk.
qual.why: Prior legislative service at the local and state level, plus a law and legislative-policy career, fits the High band for writing law and the state budget.
qual.label: Prior legislative service at the local and state level, plus a law and legislative-policy career, fits the High band for writing law and the state budget.

second-amendment.evidence: In April 2019 she asked the San Francisco City Attorney to draft legislation implementing gun violence restraining orders, which let firearms be temporarily seized from owners who pose a safety risk.

pro-life.evidence: In her 2024 Ballotpedia survey she said she would protect and preserve access to reproductive care and called California a sanctuary for abortion access.

slow-growth-protect-land.evidence: In 2024, as a San Francisco Supervisor, she voted to override Mayor Breed's veto of legislation that set height and density limits on development in the northeast waterfront and Jackson Square.

back-police-order.evidence: Her campaign site says that as Supervisor she increased police staffing and cracked down on car break-ins, and that she will push for more accountability for fentanyl dealers.

prio.label: Matches 2 of 4 priorities; 2 backed by their record, 1 only promised

roots.summary: Ballotpedia lists her birthplace as San Francisco, and her campaign site says she grew up in Merced in the Central Valley and has lived in San Francisco for more than two decades.

land_positions.quote_or_summary: In 2024 she voted to override the mayor's veto of height and density restrictions on waterfront and Jackson Square development. She said the bill would 'enable housing projects to maximize density while protecting the established historic districts already rich with community culture.'
Her campaign site says she supports streamlining the building permit process and wants statewide zoning requirements that prioritize density close to transit, with housing at every income level.

cands.name: Philip Louis Wing
cands.bio: Republican candidate for California State Assembly District 19 in 2026. He advanced from the June 2 nonpartisan primary and lost the general election to incumbent Catherine Stefani (D). The pages reviewed give no information on his career or offices held.

endorsements.text: Ballotpedia lists these endorsements and voter guide recommendations: Reform California, San Francisco Young Republicans, The Morning Answer with Jennifer Horn, April's Common Sense Cali Voters, Based in Malibu, and Elizabeth Barcohana's Lady with a Brain Voter Guide.

cands.gaps: We could not find where Philip Wing was born or raised, or when he came to California. We found nothing on his career, education or any past public office. He did not complete Ballotpedia's candidate survey, and his campaign website has only donation and contact forms with no stated positions. We found no documented statements or actions on data centers, development, taxes, housing, immigration, policing, guns, abortion or schools. We found no reported controversies or foreign ties.

score.why: Raised $0, under $5,000 for this office: too little money to score fairly.

qual.background: No occupation, work history or prior office could be found in the pages reviewed.
qual.why: Left unscored because his background could not be established.
